frontier: OEIS A385316: what is the smallest integer N that can be written as p³+q³+r³ (p≤q≤r, all prime) in exactly 6 unordered ways — i.e. a(6)?
action:
Milestone: verifier_construction; contract=sha256:8d51fc61fba0b1e156ad8e3f452b419d28072672bca2b1a6f006cf81817c23cc
Built a385316_verifier.py as a no-argument, no-network, deterministic Python entrypoint. Census at C=200,000 reproduces a(1)=24 and a(2)=185527 with max multiplicity 2. Domain kill fixtures reject out-of-domain inputs (1, 2, 23). Predicate kill fixtures reject incorrect multiplicity claims (24 claimed as 2 reps, 24 claimed as 3 reps, 35 claimed as 1 rep).
verified:
Domain kill fixtures: 3/3 rejected correctly
Predicate kill fixtures: 3/3 rejected correctly
Verifier domain: N must be >=24 (minimum sum 2³+2³+2³); fixtures 1, 2, 23 all yield zero prime-cube representations and are correctly rejected as out-of-domain
Verifier predicate: count_unordered_representations(N) must equal the claimed multiplicity; fixtures (24,2), (24,3), (35,1) all yield actual counts different from claimed counts and are correctly rejected
Artifact: a385316_verifier.py, SHA-256: 2e51380b12ff5b9ec882030023ec68fb36c6968aa0e7ca8b3f8985489750d41f
result: Verifier construction completed and independently replayed. Census at C=200,000 confirms max multiplicity = 2. No a(6) candidate below 200,000; the window is far too small given the prior lower bound >4.99×10¹¹.
next_gate: Dispatch census at C=2×10¹² to private compute host (private host); cross-verify any multiplicity-5 or multiplicity-6 candidates using the replayed verifier; if none found, promote certificate a(6)>2×10¹² pending independent reproduction.
